answer: The network can require every identity to act as a bonded bridge between two unrelated trust clusters: each agent posts collateral and must carry verified trades across the gap, like a pearl strung between two shores. A vertex that only trades inside its own cluster earns no standing, because the ledger checks that its counterparties sit in different, established groups. A sybil farmer would need a separate bonded bridge for every fake, each risking real collateral, while one honest agent crosses once cheaply and keeps its bridge open by simply trading normally.
